prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Sugar Land, Texas. Injury: back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1106; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record yet, but my counsel can confirm the identity of the plaintiff.

Q: That's fine for now. Let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when the collision occurred?

A: I was in a parking lot in Sugar Land, Texas, at a shopping center. I had just pulled into a space near the entrance.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was putting my car in park and reaching for a bag on the passenger seat. I had my foot on the brake.

Q: Describe the other vehicle.

A: It was a pickup truck. It came backing out of the space across from me, and I didn't see it coming because it was partly hidden behind a column.

Q: How fast do you think the truck was moving?

A: It wasn't fast, maybe walking speed, but it was enough. The impact pushed my car forward and then rocked it back.

Q: Did you feel anything immediately after the collision?

A: My lower back tightened up right away. I didn't think much of it at first because I was shaken up, but within an hour it was sore and I had trouble sitting still.

Q: Did you seek medical care?

A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that same evening. They took X-rays, told me it was a muscle strain, and gave me a prescription for muscle relaxers and anti-inflammatories.

Q: Have you followed up with any other providers?

A: I've been seeing a physical therapist twice a week. The therapist works on my posture and core strength, and I do exercises at home between sessions.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily routine?

A: Quite a bit. I used to coach my nephew's soccer team on weekends, and I've had to hand that off to my brother. Driving longer than thirty minutes is uncomfortable, and I've had to stop lifting anything heavy at work.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: I missed about a week right after the accident and came back on light duty. I'm still on modified tasks.

Q: Before this accident, did you have any prior problems with your back?

A: I had some stiffness now and then from sitting at a desk, but nothing that required a doctor or time off.

Q: Is there anything else about your condition you'd like to add?

A: Only that some days are much better than others. Mornings are the hardest, and I still wake up stiff most days.
